label: def:skein-binding-lagrangian
title: Skein binding Lagrangian for multi-nucleon links
html:
Definition. Let L = Z\mathfrak{p} \oplus N\mathfrak{n} be a multi-nucleon Hopf link with Z protons, N neutrons, and A = Z + N. The canonical binding Lagrangian is the categorical action \mathfrak{S}_q evaluated on L:

  \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{bind}}[L]
  = 
  \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{qCLT}}
  - \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Coulomb}}.

Each term arises from the exact evaluation of the topological trace on the link components, without empirical liquid-drop parameters:

  1. Strong Binding (q-CLT/JSJ volume term). The strong force contribution evaluates strictly from the Hecke channel traces. As established in q-CLT mass scaling, the Jaco–Shalen–Johannson decomposition yields an additive scaling for the strong binding:

      \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{qCLT}}
  = \alpha \sum_i \ln\lvert V_i\rvert,

    where \alpha = \mathfrak{m}_e / (q_0(q_0-1)) is the rigid substrate scale (built from CAL-1 \mathfrak{m}_e and CAL-2 q_0), and V_i are the two-nucleon sub-braid Markov traces for each bond type. This carries no empirical parameter beyond that calibration scale, and is intended to replace the empirical Bethe-Weizsäcker volume, surface, asymmetry, and pairing terms — but that replacement is not a completed closure: the per-isotope binding magnitude (\Delta_\lambda) is open, so its empirical accuracy against AME is not established here.

  2. Coulomb Repulsion. Each proton--proton crossing acquires a q-deformed wedge product asymmetry. The categorical difference between identical-chirality crossings (coefficient q) and mixed crossings evaluates directly to the electrostatic penalty. As mapped by the \mathrm{U}(1) sub-action:

      \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Coulomb}} = E_C(Z, A),

    which recovers the standard \approx 0.71\, Z(Z-1)/A^{1/3} MeV Coulomb energy from the \mathrm{U}(1) sub-action. A witness now exists: mirror-split-continuum-em, computed by coulomb_energy.py with zero fitted constants — the fine-structure constant from the derived trace ratio 1/(q_0 [9]_q [10]_q) and the length from the CAL-3 scale \hbar c / \mathfrak{m}_\pi, not the empirical r_0. On the mirror pair it gives \Delta E_C \approx 0.847 MeV against an observed 0.764 MeV, i.e. +10.9\%.

    Two steps in that recovery are selections rather than derivations, and the producer flags both in its own comments. The A^{1/3} packing law is not derived: solving for the exponent against measured radii gives 0.43 at ^3\mathrm{H} and 0.53 at ^3\mathrm{He}, so the residual is a radius that is roughly a fifth too small rather than a small correction. The uniform-sphere geometry factor 3/5 is likewise a choice whose alternatives bracket the answer (3/5 \to 0.849, 1/2 \to 0.707, against 0.764 observed). So the match is a genuine zero-parameter evaluation, not yet a categorical derivation of a_C.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs—real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical/q-deformation identities it relies upon remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
